text:
sam_sales: FYI - Solace Inc POC showing TTFT jumps during interactive demo. Expected ~120ms, seeing 250-800ms. They asked about Dedicated pricing and security checklist. Can we triage?

raja_eng: What model + client? sample payload?

sam_sales: model=redwood-13b-llm, streaming over websocket, prompt ~40 tokens, max_new_tokens=200. Client uses a custom SDK.

kelly_sre: Quick glance at our logs for their route: high `batcher.dispatch_delay` and many single-request batches. Also kv_cache.hit rate is ~10% for their session.

nova_support: They sent a wrapper that adds per-request timestamp meta in the prompt. That kills prefix caching. Also header `X-Batch-Disable: true` present.

raja_eng: Two immediate asks for customer: remove the header, stop injecting unique salts in the prompt. For hosted POC we can also enable route prefix_cache and lower batching.max_latency_ms to 35ms with target_batch_size 6.

kelly_sre: I rolled a canary with prefix_cache=true and batching.target=6 for their POC route and pushed a quick warmup. Median TTFT on canary dropped to ~130ms. Logs show first few calls still kv_cache.miss then kv_cache.hit.

elaine_sec: Security notes: they want KMS and confirmation of no retention for POC. We can set data_retention_days=0 and offer a limited KMS flow. I'll send the short checklist.

sam_sales: Customer insists on streaming. Can we preserve streaming but get good TTFT?

raja_eng: Yes — keep streaming but use the warmup + prefix cache and ask client to use a stable session preface (identical across requests) so KV can be reused. Also recommend client concurrency 3-5 to allow aggregation.

nova_support: Warmup snippet I gave them: 4 quick non-streaming calls with stable prefix 20s before session. That reliably seeds KV.

kelly_sre: Deploy-bot: canary deploy started for solace-poc @ 2024-09-05T10:42Z, health checks green.

sam_sales: I'll coordinate a live window with Solace CTO tomorrow. Please standby.

deploy-bot: Can confirm canary health and metrics dashboard link shared.
